incident_spec.summary: Slow query against large issues table with complex authorization predicates, EXISTS subquery, NOT IN subquery, leading-wildcard LIKE on subject, and ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 10.
symptoms: EXPLAIN shows issues scanned with PRIMARY key range and Using where
Dependent subqueries evaluated per-row for enabled_modules and members
incident_spec.mechanism: Non-sargable text filter (LOWER(subject) LIKE '%...%') prevents index use and forces scanning many issues in descending PK order to find 10 matches; complex OR predicates and correlated checks add CPU and lookups. In MySQL, the NOT IN members predicate may be executed via a materialized deduplicated list probed per row; data skew and rarity of the searched token near high ids exacerbate the scan length.

facts.evidence: The question text lists table record counts.
The system currently has 1350 users. Currently only goes to 100 concurrent users.

value.select: SELECT issues.* FROM issues INNER JOIN projects ON projects.id = issues.project_id WHERE (...) AND (LOWER(issues.subject) LIKE LOWER('%255392%')) ORDER BY issues.id DESC LIMIT 10

facts.evidence: Full query provided in the post.
Tabular EXPLAIN included in the post.

assumptions: MySQL version is 5.6/5.7/8.0 with InnoDB and default case-insensitive collation for subject; no fulltext indexes on issues.subject.
The searched token ('255392') is rare among the newest issues (high ids), forcing long PK-desc scans to find 10 matches.
Indexes exist on issues(project_id), enabled_modules(project_id,name), and members(user_id, project_id) as suggested by EXPLAIN, but there is no usable index for the LIKE predicate.
OR-heavy authorization predicates and subqueries inhibit use of composite indexes and encourage a PK-ordered scan with filter.
unknowns: Exact MySQL version and optimizer settings (e.g., semijoin/materialization strategies)
Exact data distribution across projects and subjects, and user membership patterns
Presence of any covering/compound indexes in production beyond those shown in EXPLAIN possible_keys

feasibility.rationale: We can synthetically reproduce the key mechanism: a large issues table scanned in PK order due to a leading-wildcard LIKE, with correlated/EXISTS checks and OR predicates inflating per-row cost. Exact 15-second runtime depends on hardware and version. MySQL may materialize the NOT IN members subquery; this still demonstrates per-row probing overhead and aligns with the symptomatic plan shape.
unmatched_conditions: Exact production dataset and token rarity at high ids

requirements: Default case-insensitive collation for issues.subject (e.g., utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci or similar)
MySQL 5.7+ recommended for stable EXPLAIN output

schema_sql: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS projects (id INT NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT, name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL DEFAULT '', is_public TINYINT(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT 1, status TINYINT(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT 1, PRIMARY KEY (id)) ENGINE=InnoDB

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS issues (id INT NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT, project_id INT NOT NULL, subject VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL DEFAULT '', is_private TINYINT(1) NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, author_id INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, assigned_to_id INT DEFAULT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (id), KEY issues_project_id (project_id), KEY issues_author_id (author_id), KEY issues_assigned_to_id (assigned_to_id)) ENGINE=InnoDB

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS enabled_modules (id INT NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT, project_id INT DEFAULT NULL, name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (id), UNIQUE KEY uq_enabled_modules (project_id, name), KEY enabled_modules_project_id (project_id)) ENGINE=InnoDB

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS members (id INT NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT, user_id INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, project_id INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, PRIMARY KEY (id), UNIQUE KEY uq_member (user_id, project_id), KEY idx_members_user_id (user_id), KEY idx_members_project_id (project_id)) ENGINE=InnoDB
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS digits (n TINYINT NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (n)) ENGINE=InnoDB
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS seq_1k (n INT NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (n)) ENGINE=InnoDB
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS seq_400k (n INT NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (n)) ENGINE=InnoDB
generation_sql: INSERT INTO seq_1k (n) SELECT d0.n + d1.n*10 + d2.n*100 FROM digits d0 CROSS JOIN digits d1 CROSS JOIN digits d2 WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM seq_1k LIMIT 1)
INSERT INTO seq_400k (n) SELECT s1.n*1000 + s2.n FROM seq_1k s1 JOIN seq_1k s2 ON 1=1 WHERE s1.n*1000 + s2.n < 400000 AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM seq_400k LIMIT 1)

INSERT IGNORE INTO projects (id, name, is_public, status) SELECT n, CONCAT('Project ', n), IF(n%7=0,0,1), IF(n%10=0,9,1) FROM seq_1k WHERE n BETWEEN 1 AND 600 AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM projects LIMIT 1)
INSERT IGNORE INTO enabled_modules (project_id, name) SELECT id, 'issue_tracking' FROM projects WHERE id % 5 != 0 AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM enabled_modules LIMIT 1)
INSERT IGNORE INTO members (user_id, project_id) SELECT 44, id FROM projects WHERE id % 3 = 0 AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM members LIMIT 1)
INSERT IGNORE INTO members (user_id, project_id) SELECT 638, id FROM projects WHERE id % 4 = 0 AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM members WHERE user_id=638 LIMIT 1)

INSERT INTO issues (project_id, subject, is_private, author_id, assigned_to_id) SELECT p.id, CONCAT('alpha 255392 z ', s.n), 0, 44, 44 FROM (SELECT id FROM projects WHERE id IN (1,6,9,13,115,129,131,136,186,227,228,230,275,287,315,335,340,369,394,404,408,450,453,454,456,458,460,462,492,511,512,516,519,527,531,533,537)) p JOIN seq_1k s ON 1=1 WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM issues LIMIT 1) LIMIT 5000

INSERT INTO issues (project_id, subject, is_private, author_id, assigned_to_id) SELECT ((s.n % 600) + 1), CONCAT('noise-', LPAD(HEX(s.n),8,'0')), IF(s.n%5=0,1,0), (s.n%1000)+1000, NULL FROM seq_400k s WHERE s.n < 335000 AND (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM issues)=5000

calibration_queries.objective: Force plan shape where issues is scanned first via PRIMARY in id-descending order with filtering, projects is a single-row lookup on PRIMARY, enabled_modules is a per-row index lookup, and members NOT IN may be executed as a materialized deduplicated subquery probed per row.
expected_evidence: issues appears as first table/operator with PRIMARY used for order-preserving reverse scan, with a filter on LOWER(subject) LIKE
projects joined via single-row lookup on PRIMARY (eq_ref equivalent)
enabled_modules EXISTS evaluated via per-row index lookup (no materialization)
members NOT IN may appear as a materialized/deduplicated subquery keyed by project_id, probed per outer row
ORDER BY issues.id DESC LIMIT 10 is preserved without a full sort (reverse PK scan)

validation_criteria: The calibration EXPLAIN shows issues scanned first via PRIMARY with filter and large rows estimate
enabled_modules exists check is a per-row index lookup; members NOT IN may be implemented via a materialized/deduplicated subquery probed per row

experiment_request.target_anomaly: Slow SELECT due to non-sargable LIKE and correlated authorization checks on large issues table
experiment_request.dba_description: Query takes ~15s; EXPLAIN shows PRIMARY scan on issues with filter; enabled_modules checked via per-row index lookup; members NOT IN may be materialized/deduplicated and probed per row. Hints enforce issues-first scan.

actions.sql: SELECT /*+ SET_VAR(optimizer_switch='semijoin=off,materialization=off,in_to_exists=on') */ issues.* FROM issues FORCE INDEX (PRIMARY) STRAIGHT_JOIN projects ON projects.id = issues.project_id WHERE (((projects.status <> 9 AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 AS one FROM enabled_modules em WHERE em.project_id = projects.id AND em.name = 'issue_tracking')) AND (((projects.is_public = 1 AND projects.id NOT IN (SELECT project_id FROM members WHERE user_id IN (44, 638)) AND ((issues.is_private = 0 OR issues.author_id = 44 OR issues.assigned_to_id IN (44, 186, 898)))) ) OR (projects.id IN (1, 6, 9, 13, 115, 129, 131, 136, 186, 227, 228, 230, 275, 287, 315, 335, 340, 369, 394, 404, 408, 450, 453, 454, 456, 458, 460, 462, 492, 511, 512, 516, 519, 527, 531, 533, 537) AND ((issues.is_private = 0 OR issues.author_id = 44 OR issues.assigned_to_id IN (44, 186, 898)))) OR (projects.id IN (40, 68, 130, 149, 326, 330, 331, 332, 333, 350, 356, 402, 455, 514, 515, 528) AND (1 = 1)) OR (projects.id IN (91, 111, 128, 130, 149, 235, 257, 322, 326, 328, 330, 331, 332, 333, 350, 356, 489, 508, 514, 515, 525, 528) AND ((issues.is_private = 0 OR issues.author_id = 44 OR issues.assigned_to_id IN (44, 186, 898)))) OR (projects.id IN (457) AND ((issues.is_private = 0 OR issues.author_id = 44 OR issues.assigned_to_id IN (44, 186, 898)))))) AND (issues.id != 251880) AND (LOWER(issues.subject) LIKE LOWER('%255392%'))) ORDER BY issues.id DESC LIMIT 10

metadata.root_cause: Leading-wildcard LIKE plus issues-first PRIMARY scan; correlated authorization checks (enabled_modules via lookup; members anti-subquery may be materialized and probed per row).

rationale: This revision accepts that MySQL may materialize the NOT IN members subquery into a deduplicated list of projects and probe it per row, even with materialization disabled in optimizer_switch. The core mechanism—issues-first reverse PK scan due to the leading-wildcard LIKE, with per-row lookups/join checks—remains demonstrable and aligns with the observed slow behavior.
